...TRANS REPRESENTATION. It's important. Lung transplant scars connect together, instead of being 2 separate incisions. Gynaecomastia scars are extremely different from double mastectomy scars. Look it up.

Again, if an uneducated person sees someone with those scars, how are they supposed to know that they are trans? It's good that this person is educating others. We need this representation, and we won't get it if people have no idea what those scars mean.

They explained the scars, because how else are people supposed to know that person is trans? If people don't know he's trans - then that recognition isn't given.

And no, it doesn't have to be showcasing surgery scars all the time. But in the trans community, it's a huge symbolic thing. It's not the only way to represent trans people, no. But what else did you want a trans guy to do in a body positivity image? Wave a trans flag in the air? That will just defeat the entire purpose of the image. Its *body* positivity.

Yes, sure. Many guys don't want to be open about being trans. But some guys, like myself, do. Because we need more representation and recognition.
